questions.question: You are onboarding an AI agent into your team's CI/CD pipeline. Which of the following is the BEST first step?
options: Configure the agent with full repository write access immediately
Identify the specific SDLC steps the agent will perform and define clear success criteria
Allow the agent to reason freely across all pipeline stages without constraints
Deploy the agent to production before testing in staging
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Identify the specific SDLC steps the agent will perform and define clear success criteria

questions.question: Which of the following is a common **anti-pattern** when integrating agents into the SDLC?
options: Scoping agent actions to a specific branch
Defining explicit inputs and outputs for each agent task
Allowing an agent to perform planning and execution in a single undifferentiated step
Requiring agent plans to be validated before execution
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Allowing an agent to perform planning and execution in a single undifferentiated step

questions.question: An agent is configured to plan a refactoring task and then immediately execute it without review. What is the PRIMARY risk of this configuration?
options: The agent may produce logs that are too verbose
Planning errors propagate directly into code changes before they can be caught
The agent will be unable to create pull requests
The agent's memory will expire during execution
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Planning errors propagate directly into code changes before they can be caught

questions.question: Your organization wants agents to operate autonomously but with human oversight for high-risk actions. Which configuration approach best achieves this?
options: Disable all human intervention to maximize delivery speed
Require human approval for every single agent action
Plan and implement graduated autonomy levels with guardrails based on risk
Allow agents to self-determine when human approval is needed
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Plan and implement graduated autonomy levels with guardrails based on risk

questions.question: An agent is producing outputs that are difficult to audit after the fact. What should you configure to address this?
options: Increase the agent's memory allocation
Configure the agent to produce inspectable artifacts within standard development tooling
Switch the agent to a different LLM model
Reduce the number of tools available to the agent
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Configure the agent to produce inspectable artifacts within standard development tooling

questions.question: You want to prevent an agent from taking any action until a structured plan has been reviewed and approved. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
options: Set the agent's output format to plain text
Configure the agent to output a structured plan and implement a validation gate before execution
Reduce the agent's context window size
Allow the agent to proceed if no feedback is received within 5 minutes
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Configure the agent to output a structured plan and implement a validation gate before execution

questions.question: When selecting tools for an AI agent, what is the primary consideration?
options: Use as many tools as possible to maximize agent capability
Only use tools that were released in the last 12 months
Identify which tools are specifically required for the agent's defined tasks
Avoid any tools that require network access
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Identify which tools are specifically required for the agent's defined tasks

questions.question: You need to add an external data source capability to a GitHub Copilot agent. What is the recommended approach using the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
options: Hard-code the data source credentials directly into the agent's prompt
Add an MCP server as a tool to the agent
Create a separate agent for each data source
Use environment variables to pass data directly to the LLM
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Add an MCP server as a tool to the agent

questions.question: When configuring an MCP server for a GitHub agent, which security configuration is MOST important to implement?
options: Enable all available MCP tools by default to improve agent flexibility
Configure MCP allow lists to restrict which tools and servers the agent can access
Set the MCP server to public access to allow cross-organization use
Disable MCP logging to improve performance
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Configure MCP allow lists to restrict which tools and servers the agent can access

questions.question: An agent needs to be restricted so it can only read and write to a single repository. Which configuration achieves this?
options: Configure the agent's scope to a specific repository and apply least-privilege permissions
Deploy the agent on a separate virtual machine
Limit the agent's context window to 2,000 tokens
Use a separate GitHub account for the agent
questions.explanation: Correct answer: A) Configure the agent's scope to a specific repository and apply least-privilege permissions

questions.question: You want an agent to automatically trigger on pull requests in a CI workflow. What should you configure?
options: A scheduled cron job that checks for open PRs every hour
Configure the agent to be invoked in a CI workflow triggered by pull request events
Manually run the agent each time a PR is opened
Use a webhook that emails the agent
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Configure the agent to be invoked in a CI workflow triggered by pull request events

questions.question: An agent attempting a file change fails due to a permissions error. What is the BEST response strategy?
options: Retry the action indefinitely until it succeeds
Log the error and silently skip the action
Implement error handling with a defined escalation path and rollback capability
Increase the agent's permission scope automatically
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Implement error handling with a defined escalation path and rollback capability

questions.question: You are configuring an agent to work across multiple branches in a repository. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?
options: Give the agent global write access to all branches
Configure branch-based scope to limit the agent's actions to relevant branches
Disable branch protection rules while the agent is running
Force all agent changes directly to the main branch
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Configure branch-based scope to limit the agent's actions to relevant branches

questions.question: An agent successfully creates a branch and makes code changes but then fails while opening a pull request. What should your implementation include to handle this?
options: No special handling — the user should manually create the PR
Retry logic and rollback procedures, with an escalation path if recovery fails
Delete the branch and restart the entire task
Increase the timeout value for the PR creation step
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Retry logic and rollback procedures, with an escalation path if recovery fails

questions.question: An agent is tasked with a multi-step code migration that may take several hours. Midway through, the execution is interrupted. What memory strategy should be implemented?
options: Restart the agent from the beginning each time it is interrupted
Use only in-context (short-term) memory
Capture task progress and decisions as durable artifacts to enable resumption
Require a human to manually record the agent's progress
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Capture task progress and decisions as durable artifacts to enable resumption

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes "context drift" in agentic AI systems?
options: When an agent uses too many tools simultaneously
When an agent's execution diverges from its prior decisions or task intent over time
When an agent's memory is stored in an external database
When two agents share the same context window
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) When an agent's execution diverges from its prior decisions or task intent over time

questions.question: You need an agent to remember user preferences across multiple sessions. Which memory type is MOST appropriate?
options: Short-term in-context memory
Long-term or external memory that persists across sessions
No memory — agents should start fresh each session
Branch-scoped memory that resets on merge
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Long-term or external memory that persists across sessions

questions.question: An agent is sharing state with another agent in a multi-agent workflow. What is the PRIMARY risk to manage?
options: The agents may generate too many log entries
Conflicting or stale context leading to inconsistent decisions
The agents may use the same tool twice
The shared state may consume too much CPU
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Conflicting or stale context leading to inconsistent decisions

questions.question: When should memory pruning rules be applied in an agent's memory strategy?
options: Only when the agent encounters an error
Never — all memory should be preserved indefinitely
According to defined expiration policies to prevent stale information from influencing decisions
Only when an agent is retired
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) According to defined expiration policies to prevent stale information from influencing decisions

questions.question: An agent resumes a long-running task but begins making decisions that contradict its earlier work. What mechanism should be in place to prevent this?
options: Longer context windows
Drift detection logic and correction mechanisms that compare current state to prior decisions
Switching to a more powerful LLM
Resetting all memory before each step
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Drift detection logic and correction mechanisms that compare current state to prior decisions

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a **quantitative** evaluation signal for an agent?
options: A developer's subjective rating of code quality
The percentage of agent-generated PRs that pass CI checks without modification
Whether the agent's output "feels right" to the reviewer
Team satisfaction surveys
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) The percentage of agent-generated PRs that pass CI checks without modification

questions.question: An agent is consistently selecting the wrong tool for a given task. What is the MOST likely root cause?
options: Memory expiration policy is too aggressive
The agent's instructions do not clearly define when each tool should be used
The agent is missing long-term memory
The CI workflow trigger is misconfigured
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) The agent's instructions do not clearly define when each tool should be used

questions.question: After reviewing agent logs, you discover that an agent failed because it acted on outdated context. How should this failure be classified?
options: Reasoning error
Tool misconfiguration
Context or environment issue
Network failure
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Context or environment issue

questions.question: You want to generate evaluation signals for your agent automatically during CI runs. Which approach is MOST aligned with the GH-600 exam objectives?
options: Have developers manually review every agent output
Use automated scanning tools to generate evaluation signals during pipeline execution
Compare agent outputs to competitors' agents
Run the agent on production traffic and gather feedback after the fact
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Use automated scanning tools to generate evaluation signals during pipeline execution

questions.question: An agent produces correct outputs in testing but consistently fails in production. After analysis, you determine the agent is receiving different inputs in each environment. How should you tune the agent?
options: Deploy the same test inputs to production
Disable the agent in production until inputs are identical to test
Revise the agent's instructions and constraints to handle environment-specific input variability
Increase the agent's memory allocation
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Revise the agent's instructions and constraints to handle environment-specific input variability

questions.question: When tuning an agent based on evaluation results, which combination of levers is MOST comprehensive?
options: Only modify the LLM model used
Revise instructions, refine memory usage, and adjust tool access as needed
Delete and rebuild the agent from scratch
Only modify the CI pipeline triggers
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Revise instructions, refine memory usage, and adjust tool access as needed

questions.question: An agent is performing well on most tasks but fails on edge cases involving complex reasoning chains. What is the BEST first tuning action?
options: Add more tools to the agent
Extend the agent's token limit
Analyze traces and plans from failed runs to identify where reasoning breaks down, then revise instructions
Switch to a different agent orchestration pattern
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Analyze traces and plans from failed runs to identify where reasoning breaks down, then revise instructions

questions.question: You are designing a workflow where three specialized agents must work in parallel on independent subtasks and then merge their results. Which orchestration pattern should you apply?
options: Sequential chaining — agents run one after another
Parallel execution with agent isolation and a merge/aggregation step
Single-agent execution with multiple tool calls
Human-in-the-loop for all three agents simultaneously
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Parallel execution with agent isolation and a merge/aggregation step

questions.question: Two agents are both attempting to modify the same file in a repository. What is this type of conflict called, and how should it be resolved?
options: A memory collision — resolved by clearing agent memory
An overlapping code change conflict — resolved by configuring agent isolation and conflict detection
A tool misuse error — resolved by disabling file write tools
A context drift — resolved by resetting both agents
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) An overlapping code change conflict — resolved by configuring agent isolation and conflict detection

questions.question: You need to audit what decisions were made across a multi-agent workflow that ran last week. What should have been configured in advance to support this?
options: Each agent should have had verbose console logging only
The workflow should have been configured to produce artifacts documenting key decisions, handoffs, and outcomes
A developer should have watched the workflow run in real time
The agents should have emailed status updates
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) The workflow should have been configured to produce artifacts documenting key decisions, handoffs, and outcomes

questions.question: An agent in a multi-agent workflow produces no output and stops responding. How should the system respond?
options: Continue the workflow and skip the failed agent's contribution
Detect the stalled execution, trigger a recovery pattern (such as rollback or human-in-the-loop), and alert operators
Restart all agents in the workflow from the beginning
Increase the timeout for the stalled agent indefinitely
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Detect the stalled execution, trigger a recovery pattern (such as rollback or human-in-the-loop), and alert operators

questions.question: You want to add a new specialized agent to an existing multi-agent workflow without disrupting currently running executions. What is the BEST approach?
options: Shut down the entire workflow, add the agent, and restart
Add the new agent to the workflow definition using a non-breaking update pattern, ensuring it does not interfere with active executions
Deploy the new agent to a completely separate workflow
Require all active executions to complete before making any changes
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Add the new agent to the workflow definition using a non-breaking update pattern, ensuring it does not interfere with active executions

questions.question: An agent that was part of a multi-agent workflow is being retired. What must be preserved to maintain workflow integrity?
options: The agent's in-context memory only
Nothing — retiring an agent removes all associated data
Auditability records and workflow continuity for downstream agents
The agent's tool configuration only
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) Auditability records and workflow continuity for downstream agents

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of post-hoc analysis in multi-agent workflows?
options: Previewing agent behavior before deployment
Reviewing logs, artifacts, and operational signals after execution to understand and improve multi-agent behavior
Testing agents in a sandbox environment
Monitoring agents in real time during execution
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Reviewing logs, artifacts, and operational signals after execution to understand and improve multi-agent behavior

questions.question: Your organization has a compliance policy requiring that production database schema changes never be made without a DBA review. How should this be enforced for agents?
options: Train developers to remind the agent not to make schema changes
Block schema change actions that violate the compliance policy and require explicit authorization before proceeding
Allow agents to make schema changes and review them afterward
Limit agents to read-only database access for all operations
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Block schema change actions that violate the compliance policy and require explicit authorization before proceeding

questions.question: An agent is tasked with deleting test data as part of a cleanup workflow. This action is irreversible. What guardrail should be applied?
options: Allow the deletion automatically since it is only test data
Require explicit human authorization before executing any irreversible action
Log the deletion after it occurs
Retry the deletion if it fails the first time
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Require explicit human authorization before executing any irreversible action

questions.question: Which principle should guide how permissions are assigned to agents?
options: Maximum privilege — agents should be able to do anything a senior engineer can do
Least-privilege — scope permissions to only what is required for the agent's defined tasks
Role inheritance — agents automatically inherit the permissions of the user who created them
Dynamic escalation — agents request elevated permissions when needed
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Least-privilege — scope permissions to only what is required for the agent's defined tasks

questions.question: You are classifying agent actions to determine which require human intervention. An agent wants to merge a PR to the main branch of a production repository. How should this action be classified?
options: Low risk — no human intervention required
Medium risk — log it but allow automatic execution
High risk — require explicit human authorization due to production impact
No risk — merging is always safe in agentic workflows
questions.explanation: Correct answer: C) High risk — require explicit human authorization due to production impact

questions.question: Your team wants agents to operate as autonomously as possible without compromising security. What is the BEST approach to balancing speed and safety?
options: Remove all guardrails to maximize delivery speed
Assign autonomy levels based on risk classification, minimizing approvals that do not materially reduce risk
Require human approval for every agent action regardless of risk
Allow agents to self-elevate their autonomy level based on task complexity
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Assign autonomy levels based on risk classification, minimizing approvals that do not materially reduce risk

questions.question: An agent attempts to push directly to a protected branch, violating your organization's security policy. What should happen?
options: The agent should succeed and log the policy violation for later review
The action should be blocked immediately with an appropriate error returned to the agent
A developer should be paged to manually approve the push
The branch protection rule should be temporarily suspended for the agent
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) The action should be blocked immediately with an appropriate error returned to the agent

questions.question: A developer reports that an agent "went off-track" and began performing actions unrelated to its assigned task. Which combination of controls would BEST prevent this?
options: Increase the agent's token limit and add more tools
Define clear inputs, outputs, and success criteria; validate agent plans before execution; and implement scope constraints
Use a more powerful LLM
Add long-term memory to the agent
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Define clear inputs, outputs, and success criteria; validate agent plans before execution; and implement scope constraints

questions.question: Which of the following scenarios represents a valid use of **human-in-the-loop** in an agentic workflow?
options: Requiring human approval before an agent formats a comment
Requiring human approval before an agent deploys to a production environment
Requiring human approval before an agent reads a file
Requiring human approval before the agent queries a search tool
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Requiring human approval before an agent deploys to a production environment

questions.question: An agent is generating code changes across 10 repositories simultaneously in a multi-agent workflow. After deployment, a critical bug is traced to one of the agent-generated changes. What capability must have been implemented in advance to support rapid diagnosis?
options: Agent memory pruning
Traceability and accountability — inspectable artifacts and logs linking each action to a specific agent and task
MCP allow lists
Branch-based scope
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Traceability and accountability — inspectable artifacts and logs linking each action to a specific agent and task

questions.question: You are evaluating a new agent before promoting it to production. The agent performs well on average but occasionally takes destructive actions. What is the MOST appropriate next step?
options: Promote to production immediately since average performance is good
Classify the destructive actions by risk, implement guardrails to block them, and retest before promotion
Remove all tools from the agent and re-add them one by one
Reduce the agent's memory to prevent unexpected behavior
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Classify the destructive actions by risk, implement guardrails to block them, and retest before promotion

questions.question: An agent is configured to run autonomously in a CI pipeline. A deployment step begins to behave unexpectedly mid-execution. Which capability allows the system to recover without full manual intervention?
options: Increasing the CI runner's compute resources
Rollback procedures and escalation paths configured as part of the agent's error handling strategy
Switching to a different CI platform
Disabling the agent permanently
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Rollback procedures and escalation paths configured as part of the agent's error handling strategy

questions.question: A GitHub Copilot agent needs access to a third-party issue tracking system. Using MCP, what is the correct configuration approach?
options: Embed the API credentials in the agent's system prompt
Configure a remote MCP server for the issue tracking system and add it to the agent's tool registry with appropriate allow list entries
Give the agent browser access to navigate to the tracking system manually
Use a GitHub Action to sync data to a local file the agent can read
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Configure a remote MCP server for the issue tracking system and add it to the agent's tool registry with appropriate allow list entries

questions.question: Which of the following statements about agent evaluation signals is TRUE?
options: Only qualitative signals (like human ratings) are useful for evaluating agents
Evaluation signals should be aligned with development intent, not just general quality metrics
Evaluation signals are only relevant after an agent fails
Automated scanning tools cannot generate evaluation signals
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Evaluation signals should be aligned with development intent, not just general quality metrics

questions.question: In the context of GH-600, what is the primary purpose of configuring an agent to use **branch-based scope**?
options: To increase the agent's processing speed
To ensure the agent only operates within designated branches, reducing risk of unintended changes to protected code
To allow the agent to merge branches automatically
To give the agent read access to all branches in the organization
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) To ensure the agent only operates within designated branches, reducing risk of unintended changes to protected code

questions.question: An organization is deploying multiple agents that each handle different parts of the SDLC. A new compliance requirement mandates that all agent actions be attributable to a specific workflow and timestamp. Which capability directly addresses this requirement?
options: Agent memory pruning policies
Traceability and auditability through inspectable artifacts and structured logging
MCP registry configuration
Autonomy level classification
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Traceability and auditability through inspectable artifacts and structured logging

questions.question: Which of the following BEST summarizes the key principle behind responsible agentic AI development as reflected throughout the GH-600 exam objectives?
options: Agents should operate with maximum autonomy to deliver the fastest results possible
Agents should be designed with clear boundaries, observability, human oversight where appropriate, and accountability for all actions
Human oversight should be minimized to reduce workflow friction
Agent behavior should be opaque to developers to protect IP
questions.explanation: Correct answer: B) Agents should be designed with clear boundaries, observability, human oversight where appropriate, and accountability for all actions
